findings.description: For a merged session, windowStalled measures from the newest `respawn` of any kind (delivered or not) to the newest gate_result `to: merged`. fixRoundFailure, though, applies stalledAtEnd to the newest *delivered* round window it saw open. A retry round rolled back by startFixRound's undoRound still ends in a running->merged kill, and that kill is what gets measured, not the opened window's. If the retry failed before its `respawn` was appended (writeSessionProfile/launchSession throw, or a `pup kill` while the window opens), the measured span runs from round 1's last hook to the rollback. It includes the idle time while the session sat merged, so the next `pup fix` falsely climbs with reason `stall`. If the retry's kickoff was undelivered, the span is the kickoff wait of about 45s, so a real stall of round 1 is dropped.
findings.body:
**The stall bound and the window `fixRoundFailure` scores can be different windows**

In `windowStalled`, a merged session's stall is measured from `respawnAt` (the newest `respawn` of any kind) to `at` (the newest gate_result `to: merged`):

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/868db5ca4759ed34864b55ca42d28df262b25981/src/core/dashboard.service.ts#L262-L276

`fixRoundFailure` applies that boolean to a different window: the last round whose `respawn` was **delivered**. It skips an undelivered `respawn`, and a later `fix_round` with no `respawn` does not reset `opened`, so the earlier round's window stays the scored one:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/868db5ca4759ed34864b55ca42d28df262b25981/src/core/routing.utils.ts#L206-L223

A retry round that `relaunchWorker` rolls back still writes a `running -> merged` edge (`undoRound` -> `killSession`, kind `fix-round-killed`), and that edge is the `at` measured here. Two reachable cases:

1. **False climb.** Round 1 opens and is killed while busy (no stall, rung 0). Some time later (10+ minutes), `pup fix` #2 takes the edge, then `writeSessionProfile`/`launchSession` throws, or a `pup kill` lands while the window opens (`hasRowMoved`). No `respawn` is appended, and the round is undone with a `running -> merged` kill. On `pup fix` #3, `respawnAt` is still round 1's, `at` is the rollback, and `inWindow` and `from === 'running'` both hold. `endedAt - max(mtime, windowStart)` covers the gap from round 1's last hook to the rollback, which is at least `STALLED_AFTER_MS`. `fixRoundFailure` still has `opened` from round 1, so it returns `'stall'` and the retry climbs a rung that was never earned. That contradicts the `relaunchWorker` doc: "an undone round's retry climbs no higher than the round would have".
2. **Lost climb.** Round 1 is killed while stalled. `pup fix` #2 routes to rung 1 (`stall`), but its kickoff never becomes ready. That writes `respawn {delivered:false}` and then the rollback kill straight after, and the route is not stored. On `pup fix` #3, `respawnAt` is the undelivered `respawn`, so the measured span is close to zero and reads not stalled. `fixRoundFailure` ignores that `respawn` and still scores round 1's window, now without its stall, so the retry stays on rung 0.

Root cause: the window bounds (the opening `respawn` and the ending kill) are worked out twice, in `windowStalled` and in `fixRoundFailure`, and the two disagree. One fix is to have the fix-round reader report which window it opened (the index of its delivered `respawn`), then measure the stall at the first `running -> merged` edge after that index, and only when no later `fix_round` comes before it. Neither path is covered by a test: both new tests open exactly one round.

findings.description: `stalledAtEnd = false` on fixRoundFailure is a default no production caller relies on: the only one (the `read` callback in windowFailureOf) always passes both arguments. Only routing-utils.test.ts uses the default; making it required and passing `false` there removes an implicit "stall not measured" path.
